meaning:
ὀφειλέτης, -ου, ὁ
(ὀφείλω),
a debtor: with genitive (of the amount), Mat.18:24. Metaphorical, of obligation or duty in general, with reference to favours received or injury done, etc.: Mat.6:12, Rom.1:14 8:12 15:27, Gal.5:3; of sinners, in relation to God (= Heb. חַיָּב; cf. Sir (Heb.8:5) (6)), Luk.13:4.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
Or those eighteen, on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them; do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem?
I am debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish.
Yes, I testify again to every man who receives circumcision that he is a debtor to do the whole law.
